import seaborn as sns

plt.xlabel('Product')

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert date column to datetime
coffee_sales['date'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'])

# Group the data by product and calculate total sales
product_sales = coffee_sales.groupby('product')['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Create a bar chart with seaborn
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.barplot(x='product', y='total', data=product_sales)

# Set title and labels
plt.title('Total Sales by Product')
plt.xlabel('Product')
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
